extracted.intended_audience: children's book illustrators, publishers, librarians, and general readers interested in children's literature and youth media awards
extracted.subtask_description: Official rules, eligibility, and judging criteria used to select the Randolph Caldecott Medal and Caldecott Honor Books, including what constitutes a picture book, how illustrations are evaluated, who may be considered, and the committee's nomination and voting procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of the Medal
rubrics_metrics.description: The Medal is "for distinguished illustrations in a picture book and for excellence of pictorial presentation for children".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The award's goal is to recognize 'distinguished illustrations in a picture book and for excellence of pictorial presentation for children.' The Caldecott and Newbery Medals are considered the most prestigious American children's book awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a picture book
rubrics_metrics.description: A picture book provides "a visual experience. A picture book has a collective unity of storyline, theme, or concept, developed through the series of pictures" that constitute the book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility and judging assume that the book's pictures collectively develop storyline/theme/concept; the book is valued as a visual experience rather than as a work that relies primarily on other media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustrations: artistic technique
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrations are judged on their artistic technique.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artistic technique is an explicit dimension the committee evaluates when determining the 'most distinguished' picture book.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustrations: interpretation of the book's story and theme
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrations are judged on their interpretation of the book's story and theme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation considers how illustrations interpret and add meaning to the underlying story and thematic material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustrations: fit between illustrations and the story/themes
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrations are judged on the fit between the illustrations and the story and themes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges assess congruence and appropriateness of pictorial choices relative to narrative and thematic intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustrations: precision of depiction (characters, mood, elements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrations are judged on the precision of depiction of elements of the book, like characters and mood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This covers how precisely and effectively illustrations depict characters, atmosphere, setting, and other concrete elements that contribute to the book's impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustrations: service to targeted audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrations are judged on how well the illustrations serve their targeted audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee considers whether pictorial presentation meets the needs, understanding, and expectations of the intended children readers (picture books for audiences up to age 14 may be considered).

rubrics_metrics.name: Honor books same criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Honor books need to fulfill the same criteria as the Medal winner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Runners-up designated as Caldecott Honor Books are evaluated against the same illustration-focused standards as the winner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of non-illustration components
rubrics_metrics.description: Components other than illustration, including the book's text or overall design, may be considered as they affect the overall effectiveness of the book's illustrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the Medal is for illustration, judges may take into account text, layout, typography, or design insofar as they influence the pictorial presentation's effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Book must be self-contained (independent of other media)
rubrics_metrics.description: The book must be self-contained, independent of other media for its enjoyment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adaptations or works that rely on external media for full understanding are not appropriate; the picture-book experience should stand alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: illustrator citizenship/residency
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible for the Caldecott, the artist must be a US citizen or resident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only American illustrators (citizens or residents) are eligible under current rules; note that there have been public discussions about expanding eligibility internationally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: publication language and place
rubrics_metrics.description: The book must have been published in English, in the United States first, or simultaneously in other countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority is given to U.S. first publication in English; simultaneous international publication is acceptable, but later foreign-first publications are not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: age range
rubrics_metrics.description: Picture books for any audience up to the age of 14 may be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The award covers the broad picture-book age range (not limited to preschool), up through material intended for readers up to 14 years old.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee composition and selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee comprises fifteen members of ALSC: seven members are elected by the entire ALSC membership and eight, including the chairperson, are appointed by the ALSC President.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members are chosen based on their experience; consideration is given to ensure a diversity of libraries (public and school, small and large) and geographic areas are represented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomination process (committee nominations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members formally nominate seven books in three rounds over the year, and less formally recommend others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal nominations help identify contenders across the year; informal recommendations supplement the formal lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission practices (publishers sending copies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishers send copies of books to the committee; however, a book does not need to be sent to the committee to be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sending copies facilitates review (committee members received more than 700 copies each in 2009), but omission of a submitted copy does not automatically disqualify a book.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voting procedure and point system
rubrics_metrics.description: When voting, committee members list their first place, second place, and third place selections; each vote is assigned a point value (first = 4, second = 3, third = 2). The winner must receive at least eight first place votes and be at least eight points ahead of the second-place finisher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The scoring/threshold rules determine how the winner is selected during the ALSC midwinter meeting discussion and balloting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honor book selection after winner determined
rubrics_metrics.description: After a winner is selected, the committee can decide whether to award any honor books; they may be chosen from runner-ups to the winner, or be selected in a separate ballot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Number of Honor Books varies (historically between one and five). The committee has discretion in selecting honors and may use additional ballots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and meeting for final selection
rubrics_metrics.description: At ALSC's annual midwinter meeting, held in late January or early February, the committee will discuss the nominations and hold a vote on the winner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final deliberation and balloting occur at this meeting; announcement follows after the committee's decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secrecy of deliberations and announcement process
rubrics_metrics.description: The winner and honor books are kept secret until they are publicly announced, with the committee calling the winning illustrators the morning of the announcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee deliberations and results are not released in advance; historically there has been debate about making past discussions public, but as of the page's last update no change had been made.
